findings.description: そんなに可哀想なら面倒を見てあげればいい invites Maria to care for the rose if she feels so sorry for it. “Everything would be fine if they looked over this poor thing” changes the personal invitation to a collective action and an assurance of outcome.

contexts.japanese:
その中に一輪、枯れ掛けた薔薇があり、真里亞が感傷に囚われ消沈してしまう。
でも、譲治が機転を利かし、
そんなに可哀想なら面倒を見てあげればいいと飴玉の包み紙で目印を付けてあげると、すぐに機嫌を直した。
contexts.japanesePC: でも、譲治が機転を利かし、そんなに可哀想なら面倒を見てあげればいいと飴玉の包み紙で目印を付けてあげると、すぐに機嫌を直した。

その中に一輪、枯れ掛けた薔薇があり、真里亞が感傷に囚われ消沈してしまう。
でも、譲治が機転を利かし、
そんなに可哀想なら面倒を見てあげればいいと飴玉の包み紙で目印を付けてあげると、すぐに機嫌を直した。
contexts.WH: But George used his quick wits, and, saying everything would be fine if they looked over this poor thing, marked it with a candy wrapper, and immediately restored Maria's good mood.
contexts.MG:
In the midst of all this, there was a single unhealthy rose, and Maria became overwhelmed with dejection at its condition.
But George used his quick wits,
and, saying that everything would be fine if they took care of this poor thing, marked it with a candy wrapper and immediately restored Maria's good mood.
contexts.UP:
There was a single unhealthy rose among them, and Maria became overwhelmed with dejection at its state.
But George used his quick wits,
and saying she should look after it if she felt that sorry for it, he marked it with a candy wrapper, and immediately restored Maria's good mood.
contexts.note: MG retains collective they and assurance everything would be fine; UP restores individual invitation to Maria to care for the rose.

findings.sourceReading: George suggests that if she feels so sorry for it, she can look after it, then marks it with a candy wrapper and restores her mood.
findings.alternative: Looked over can loosely convey attention, and wrapper marking survives. The source does not promise everything will be fine or substitute a collective they for her care.

findings.description: The English retains the naming of the solar death day as New Year’s Eve/Samhain but drops お祝いした, that they celebrated it.

contexts.japanese:
「うん。
だから彼らは、１０月の最後に太陽は死に、死の国で体を休めて、冬至の日に再び蘇ると考えたの。
それで、太陽が一年の生涯を終えて死ぬその日を大晦日、サヴィンと呼んで、お祝いしたの」
「再び日照時間が長くなりだす冬至の日を、太陽の復活の日とする考え方はとても面白いよね。
古代の人々がいかに太陽を神聖視していたかがわかるエピソードだよ」
contexts.japanesePC: 「うん。だから彼らは、１０月の最後に太陽は死に、死の国で体を休めて、冬至の日に再び蘇ると考えたの。それで、太陽が一年の生涯を終えて死ぬその日を大晦日、サヴィンと呼んで、お祝いしたの。」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「うん。
だから彼らは、１０月の最後に太陽は死に、死の国で体を休めて、冬至の日に再び蘇ると考えたの。
それで、太陽が一年の生涯を終えて死ぬその日を大晦日、サヴィンと呼んで、お祝いしたの」
「再び日照時間が長くなりだす冬至の日を、太陽の復活の日とする考え方はとても面白いよね。
古代の人々がいかに太陽を神聖視していたかがわかるエピソードだよ」
contexts.WH: "Yes.  So they thought that at the end of October, the sun died, rested its body in the land of the dead, and then revived again at the winter solstice.  Then, they called the day that the sun ended its one year lifespan and died New Year's Eve, or Samhain."
contexts.MG:
"Yes.
So, they thought that at the end of October, the sun died, was laid to rest in the land of the dead, and was then revived at the winter solstice.
And the name they gave to the last day of their year, when the sun ended its one year lifespan and died...was Samhain, and they celebrated then."
"It's an interesting idea, to think that the sun is revived on the day of the winter solstice, when the daylight hours start to grow longer again.
It's a case that makes it clear how much the ancients regarded the sun as sacred."
contexts.UP:
"Yep.
So they thought that at the end of October, the sun died, rested its body in the land of the dead, and then revived again at the winter solstice.
And so, they celebrated the day that the sun ends its one‐year lifespan and dies, calling it New Year's Eve, or Samhain."
"That way of thinking is very interesting, to say that the sun is "revived" on the day of the winter solstice, when the daylight hours start to grow longer again.
It's an episode that makes you understand how much ancient people deified the sun."
contexts.note: Both now explicitly include celebration of the solar death day.

findings.sourceReading: In Maria’s account, the sun dies at October’s end and revives at winter solstice; people name the death day Samhain/New Year’s Eve and celebrate it.
findings.alternative: The entire discussion is about a festival, making celebration inferable. Its explicit inclusion in this historical explanation is nonetheless omitted.

それが他でもない母に踏みにじられる光景。
…それが真里亞の瞳に、消せない焼きごてを押し当てる…。

findings.sourceReading: The sweet is proof of the memory of shopping happily with mother, brief though it was.
findings.alternative: The mother-given gift and brief happy interval survive, limiting the shift. The source locates happiness in the joint shopping, not the object being fun.

findings.alternative: The surrounding repeated disgusting language makes contempt explicit in both versions. The difference is the recurrent causal blame construction rather than an invented overall hostile attitude.

findings.sourceReading: Genji predicts that Kinzo would probably keep researching until reunion with Beatrice, even if he literally became a ghost.
findings.alternative: The English also names reunion as a limit and retains “probably,” so it leaves two competing endpoints rather than simply asserting cessation at death. Nonetheless, its “until” removes the explicit persistence beyond becoming a ghost.

findings.description: 大切な機会 calls Halloween an important opportunity for witches to interact with otherworldly visitors. MG the most important chance adds a superlative ranking not stated here. UP precious opportunity preserves importance without ranking.

contexts.japanese:
「つまり、ハロウィンはこの世とあの世の交流のある時期ってわけなんだな？
それでつまり、魔女たちにとってはそういう世界の客人たちと交流できる大切な機会だったと。
そう言いたいわけか」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「つまり、ハロウィンはこの世とあの世の交流のある時期ってわけなんだな？
それでつまり、魔女たちにとってはそういう世界の客人たちと交流できる大切な機会だったと。
そう言いたいわけか」
contexts.MG:
"So Halloween is a time when those two worlds intermingle?
In other words, it's the most important chance for witches to intermingle with guests from that world.
Is that what you're trying to say?"
contexts.UP:
"So Halloween is a time when this world and that world intermingle?
So, in other words, it's a precious opportunity for witches to interact with visitors from that world.
Is that what you want to say?"

findings.alternative: Row 97 separately states that witch/demon powers are most active in October, but that does not make this earlier opportunity explicitly the most important.

findings.description: 感謝の気持ちがあってもいいわけだね allows gratitude for the harvest as a fitting interpretation of giving candy. UP the reason ... must be because ... they should be thanked strengthens this into a necessary causal explanation. MG you might say preserves the tentative allowance.

contexts.japanese:
「ハロウィンの仮装は、向こうから来る客人たちの模倣。
……つまり、彼らにお菓子を施すのは、一年の収穫への感謝の気持ちがあってもいいわけだね」
「うー！
譲治お兄ちゃんの言う通り！」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「ハロウィンの仮装は、向こうから来る客人たちの模倣。
……つまり、彼らにお菓子を施すのは、一年の収穫への感謝の気持ちがあってもいいわけだね」
「うー！
譲治お兄ちゃんの言う通り！」
contexts.MG:
"Halloween costumes imitate the guests that come from the other side.
...In other words, you might say giving out candy is a way to show gratitude for the yearly harvest."
"Uu-!
Just like George onii-chan says!"
contexts.UP:
"Halloween costumes are an imitation of the visitors from the other side.
......So, then, the reason we give candy to them must be because of a feeling that they should be thanked for the yearly harvest."
"Uu!
Just like George onii‐chan says!"

findings.alternative: George is deriving an interpretation from Maria’s account, and her agreement endorses it. The Japanese still uses permissive あってもいい rather than obligatory necessity or a uniquely established origin.

findings.description: MG changes inventing protective rituals into performing them.

contexts.japanese: そこで彼らは、これらの害を受けないようなおまじないを生み出していった。
contexts.japanesePS3: そこで彼らは、これらの害を受けないようなおまじないを生み出していった。
contexts.MG: So, in order to avoid harm, they performed rituals.
contexts.UP: So in order to avoid harm from them, the people invented protective rituals.

findings.sourceReading: 生み出していった narrates the practices being developed; original WH created enchantments and UP invented protective rituals preserve creation.
findings.alternative: Performing practices implies they exist, but does not preserve the narrated origin.

findings.description: スケールのでかい話 comments on the large scale of Maria’s account or ambition. MG detailed and impressive replaces scope with elaborateness and favorable appraisal; UP large-scale dream retains the magnitude.

contexts.japanese:
「へー…。
そいつぁ何だかスケールのでかい話だな。
……ところでベアトリーチェって誰だっけ？
……何だっけ、えっとえっと、聞いた名前だな…」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「へー…。
そいつぁ何だかスケールのでかい話だな。
……ところでベアトリーチェって誰だっけ？
……何だっけ、えっとえっと、聞いた名前だな…」
contexts.MG:
"Oh...?
That sounds pretty detailed and impressive.
...By the way, who was Beatrice again?
...Hmm, I know I've heard that name somewhere before..."
contexts.UP:
"Wow...
That's a pretty large‐scale dream.
......By the way, who was Beatrice again?
......What was it, umm, umm, I've heard that before..."

findings.alternative: Large scale can impress Battler, but detailed is a different property and the source does not explicitly praise the account as impressive.

findings.description: 全員顔を揃える means everyone meeting or gathering together. UP gather our faces mechanically translates the idiom into an unnatural physical object for gather; MG meet in person conveys the meeting.

contexts.japanese:
「そうや！
留弗夫くんの言う通りや。
……わしらが全員顔を揃えるのは年に一度しかない。
貴重な時間を大事にし、忌憚ない話し合いをせんといかん」
contexts.japanesePS3:
「そうや！
留弗夫くんの言う通りや。
……わしらが全員顔を揃えるのは年に一度しかない。
貴重な時間を大事にし、忌憚ない話し合いをせんといかん」
contexts.MG:
"Yep!
Just as Rudolf-kun says.
...This is the only time of year we can all meet in person.
We've gotta take this valuable time seriously and be frank with each other."
contexts.UP:
"Yep!
Just as Rudolf‐kun says.
......We can only gather our faces here once a year.
We've gotta value this precious time we've got, and talk together frankly."

findings.alternative: The gathering meaning remains inferable, so this is a local idiom/English expression defect rather than a changed attendee count.

findings.description: 鼻の下を伸ばした describes Hideyoshi and Rudolf’s leering or besotted expression as they watch Shannon leave. MG substitutes a general trait, had a soft spot for women, while UP turned heads supplies a neutral movement. Both weaken the immediate lustful reaction.

contexts.japanese:
「それでは、失礼いたします。
御用がありましたら、いつでもお呼び付けください」
紗音が丁寧にお辞儀して退室する。
鼻の下を伸ばした秀吉と留弗夫がそれを見送ると、
…場の空気は紗音が訪れる直前のものに逆戻りし始める。
contexts.japanesePS3:
「それでは、失礼いたします。
御用がありましたら、いつでもお呼び付けください」
紗音が丁寧にお辞儀して退室する。
鼻の下を伸ばした秀吉と留弗夫がそれを見送ると、
…場の空気は紗音が訪れる直前のものに逆戻りし始める。
contexts.MG:
"Then, if you will excuse me.
If there is anything you desire, please call for it at any time."
Shannon bowed politely and left the room.
As Hideyoshi and Rudolf, who had a soft spot for women, watched her go,
...the atmosphere in the room began to revert back to what it had been right before Shannon's visit.
contexts.UP:
"Then, if you will excuse me.
If there is anything you desire, please call for it at any time."
Shannon bowed politely and left the room.
After Hideyoshi and Rudolf watched her go with turned heads,
...the atmosphere in the room began to revert back to what it had been right before Shannon had visited.

findings.alternative: MG’s fondness for women and UP’s attention to Shannon can suggest attraction, but neither clearly preserves the depicted leering expression at this moment.

findings.description: 人影に飛びつく describes Maria leaping onto or clinging to the arriving figure. Both translations reduce this to dashing over to the figure, preserving approach but losing the physical contact. The following explanation likewise replaces jumping onto a stranger with dashing over.

contexts.japanese:
「ベアトリーチェー！！」
真里亞がその人影に飛びつく。
……普段の楼座なら、見ず知らずの人に娘が飛びつくようなことがあれば叱る。
…しかし楼座は、それを忘れて、ただただ呆然とするしかできなかった。
contexts.japanesePS3:
「ベアトリーチェー！！」
真里亞がその人影に飛びつく。
……普段の楼座なら、見ず知らずの人に娘が飛びつくようなことがあれば叱る。
…しかし楼座は、それを忘れて、ただただ呆然とするしかできなかった。
contexts.MG:
"Beatrice!!"
Maria dashed over to the shadow.
...Normally, Rosa would scold her daughter if she dashed over to someone whom she hadn't seen before and didn't know.
...But Rosa forgot to do that, was unable to do anything but stand there, stunned.
contexts.UP:
"Beatrice!!"
Maria dashed over to the figure.
......Normally, Rosa would scold her daughter if she dashed over to a complete stranger.
...But Rosa forgot about that, unable to do anything but stand there, shocked.

findings.alternative: Running up may precede an embrace, but the translated lines do not establish the contact that 飛びつく states.
